about.tagline: Software engineer, tinkerer, and builder of things that work for a long time.

beyond.title: Husband & father
beyond.text: First and foremost, I'm a husband to the best, most beautiful, smart, and funny wife I could have met, and a father to a wonderful, spunky, and frightfully intelligent boy. When he's awake, I try to spend as much time as I can with him: watching him grow, feeding him strawberries, and playing piano together.

beyond.title: Gaming
beyond.text: I've always been a gamer. It's how I unwind, and honestly, it's part of what got me into software in the first place. Long RPG session or something competitive, I'm always down.

beyond.title: Anime
beyond.text: Yeah, I watch anime. My top 10 changes every season, though One Piece is almost always number one. If you want to talk about what's airing or debate subs vs. dubs, I'm your guy.

beyond.title: Home lab
beyond.text: I run my own home lab and love experimenting with infrastructure, self-hosting, and networking, and generally seeing how things work under the hood. If it has a config file, I'm going to mess with it.

projects.name: Marbles
projects.text: A digital version of a board game invented by my mom's side of the family. It brings out the best (and worst) in everyone at family gatherings, and I've wanted to put it on a screen for years. The repo is up and waiting for me to carve out the time.

cfg.label: Complete
cfg.headline: Software Engineer & Technology Leader
cfg.summary: I use software to innovate, automate, and improve development and user experiences. My skills lie heavily in scalable, full-stack web and native applications.
cfg.intro: I'm a software engineer in West Des Moines, Iowa, with a career spent building, breaking, fixing, and shipping software across a wild range of tech stacks. These days I wear two hats: Software Consultant at Source Allies, and the entire IT department at Patient Preferred.

basics.name: Ryan Jensen
basics.label: Software Engineer & Technology Leader
basics.summary: I use software to innovate, automate, and improve development and user experiences. My skills lie heavily in scalable, full-stack web and native applications.

work.name: Source Allies
work.summary: Delivered software consulting across 4+ client engagements spanning financial services, insurance, identity management, and enterprise web platforms. Work covered full-stack development, technical delivery leadership, coaching, and generative AI.
highlights: Led internationalization of a client's customer-facing portal and outgoing email system, adding full English/French support using Vue I18n and Thymeleaf on a Vue.js frontend and Java/Spring Boot backend, covering both web pages and email layouts.
Reworked the frontend of a high-traffic identity-management application, one of the client's most performant systems.
Bootstrapped a generative AI initiative using AWS Bedrock, Python, and Node.js.
Served as technical delivery lead on a data engineering engagement using SQL Server, Databricks, and dbt, with project management and coaching responsibilities.
Contributed across engagements as needed in delivery, strategy development, product management, UX/UI, and business analysis.
Ranked #1 interviewer at Source Allies for 2025 and the first half of 2026. Interviewed 30+ candidates; about 10 were hired and are still with the company.
Mentored and taught the company's apprentices.

work.name: Patient Preferred Financial Services
work.note: Currently part-time, supporting new feature requests and regular software updates.
work.summary: The company's sole developer and IT person for its clinic payment and patient management platform, inherited from a larger development team. Report directly to leadership and own technology strategy and roadmap, budget and vendor selection, and security and compliance. Partner closely with teams at the company's software vendors, including DataX, ACHeck, and Web.com.
highlights: Cut monthly AWS costs ~91%, from ~$1,400 to ~$120, over three years of incremental modernization with Terraform, CloudFront path-based routing, and right-sized infrastructure, while improving availability, stability, and speed.

Modernized the platform from an AngularJS frontend and .NET Framework 4.5 API on Windows Server 2012 EC2 instances to React on AWS Amplify and a .NET 10 Minimal API on Elastic Beanstalk, with SQL Server moved to RDS and SQL Agent jobs replaced by EventBridge-triggered Lambda functions.
Integrated third-party software offerings with resiliency and fallback plans for critical processes, including ACH payment processing.
Handle everything from patient onboarding and document signing to customer support and keeping the lights on.

work.name: Principal Financial Group
work.summary: Upgraded legacy .NET applications and set up CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions. Supported the team on migrations from on-prem to AWS, including Lambda for serverless applications and SNS for pub/sub messaging. Reduced build times in existing pipelines by at least 80% to improve developer experience and tighten feedback loops.

work.name: Wellabe, Inc.
work.summary: Led several small teams rewriting parts or all of applications to unify the company tech stack, adopt modern frameworks and tooling, and optimize the performance of legacy software. Migrated older WPF desktop apps to Blazor web apps. Supported and improved daily business-critical batch programs. Reengineered CI/CD processes to increase developer throughput and added requirements to encourage test coverage. Built a department wiki to centralize company, department, and team documentation. Served as senior engineering mentor to 7 junior and mid-level engineers.
highlights: Led the team that owned the company's main revenue-generating software product, delivering features on request.
Responsible for every engineer on the team: trained them, answered their questions, and paired with each intern for their entire internship.

work.name: Far Reach Inc.
work.summary: Consulted on a homegrown ERP system. Implemented full-stack features and changes using Angular, RxJS, .NET, and SQL Server on a hosted Azure instance. Accelerated development using ASP.NET Boilerplate, PrimeNG, and Bootstrap.

work.name: Hy-Vee, Inc.
work.summary: Led an effort to migrate widely used code libraries from a file share to a GitHub repository with a full CI/CD pipeline, cloud artifact storage, and automated test suites. Leveraged existing CI/CD technologies to cut pipeline build times by at least 50%. Legacy applications were primarily .NET (mixed C# and VB) with WinForms frontends. Greenfield applications were built with React and RxJS on a backend of Kotlin, Spring Boot, Ktor, and GraphQL, federated into a supergraph with Apollo Federation and hosted on Google Cloud.
highlights: Served on a task force that built a Tax API to manage tax values for retail products at every Hy-Vee location (roughly 280 grocery stores and 175 convenience stores at the time).
Solved the problem of loading millions of tax records onto the servers of newly built stores: data went out in batches, with a check after each batch to confirm every item was accounted for.
Used a pub/sub architecture to release new tax values to all stores.

work.name: Stine Seed, Inc.
work.summary: Developed features for employee-facing portals used to manage seed production, packaging, and sales. Maintained a tight feedback loop with users as implementations were deployed and tested. Used Angular for the frontend and .NET Core for the backend, with CI/CD handled through custom Azure DevOps processes I built.

work.name: Brownells, Inc.
work.summary: Integrated a new third-party ERP offering with existing WMS and POS systems. Constructed message pathways and failover processes in a pub/sub architecture between all systems. The frontend was built with Razor Pages, jQuery, AJAX, and Bootstrap; the backend used .NET Framework ASP.NET APIs, with a message bus built on IBM MQ.

work.name: UPS
work.position: Package Handler → Local Sort Supervisor → Package Center Supervisor
work.summary: Promoted twice, from package handler to Package Center Supervisor. Supervised 30+ drivers and 40+ inside employees, holding workgroups accountable for safety, production, and attendance. Personally trained more than half of them and kept their certifications current.

highlights: Oversaw all delivery drivers during the day, supporting their needs, keeping every route running smoothly, and handling emergencies.
Tracked operational data including fuel usage, time card accuracy, and a continually updated map of the delivery region.
Ran the evening local sort, ensuring packages from 30+ package cars were unloaded and sorted into five outbound trailers, with small packages separated and bagged.
Handled training, terminations, and other personnel management for the sort crew.
Loaded and unloaded trucks.
Moved into international package processing, verifying packages met requirements to ship internationally by air or freight.
Trained in hazardous materials handling, classification, and proper shipping.

cfg.label: Engineering Manager
cfg.headline: Software Engineering Manager
cfg.summary: Engineering leader with 8+ years of full-stack software experience and nearly four years supervising frontline teams before that. I hire, mentor, and grow engineers, own technology strategy and budgets, and lead delivery across .NET, JVM, and JavaScript stacks on AWS and Azure.
cfg.intro: I've spent my career building, breaking, fixing, and shipping software, and these days a lot of that work is about people. I've been Source Allies' #1 interviewer, mentored apprentices and interns, and run a company's entire technology operation on my own. Before any of that, I ran sort crews and delivery routes at UPS, so leading a team isn't new to me.

cfg.intro: I love the craft. I've spent 8+ years building, breaking, fixing, and shipping software across .NET, JVM, and JavaScript stacks, and I'm happiest untangling the hard problem, modernizing the legacy system nobody wants to touch, and bringing the rest of the team along with me.
